articles.title: Tesla's Roadster event is on tonight. Here's what to expect.
articles.summary: After a two-week delay, the Tesla Roadster event is back on — for now.
articles.body:
After a two-week delay, the Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster event is back on.

This week, Tesla added a countdown clock to its Tesla Roadster website , stating that the reveal would occur at 7:55 p.m. CDT on Oct. 15, two weeks after the initial Oct. 1 reveal date. Tesla said the reveal was pushed back due to weather conditions at the demo site, SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Rocket Development and Testing facility in Waco, Texas . The event will be streamed on Tesla's X account .

Tesla stock fell almost 2% during premarket trading on Thursday.

This price reflects trading activity during the overnight session on the Blue Ocean ATS, available 8 PM to 4 AM ET, Sunday through Thursday, when regular markets are closed.

Stormy weather would've likely hampered the Roadster's rumored hovering or flying ability. The Information reported several weeks ago that the reveal event on Oct. 1 could include a demonstration of a limited-edition version of the Roadster equipped with cold-gas thrusters developed in collaboration with SpaceX ( SPCX ), possibly including airborne flight.

Tesla is asking prospective buyers to put down a $5,000 deposit, followed by a $45,000 wire transfer due within 10 days of the initial deposit.

Tesla has not said how much the new Roadster will cost, though it is expected to exceed $250,000. However, when Tesla announced the 7:55 p.m. CDT reveal time on X.com, CEO Elon Musk replied, "Timing is everything," suggesting the digits may have some meaning.

Longtime analyst and Tesla bull Pierre Ferragu suggested it could have something to do with the price, then coyly threw out the number $75,990. He later followed up with the idea that the Roadster event should start at "7:59:90." Some have suggested this could refer to the starting price of the car's base model or to a particular track time the Roadster achieved.

The original Roadster, released in 2008 and on sale until 2012, was Tesla's first-ever EV and used a Lotus Elise chassis.

Tesla announced its successor way back in 2017, took in reservations with those high deposits, and originally said deliveries would begin in 2020. Those initial reservation holders have been waiting for quite a long time.

During his appearance on the All-In Summit , Musk brought up the Tesla Roadster.

"It'll be a banger. Excitement guaranteed. Success is not guaranteed, but excitement is," he added, with All-In host Jason Calacanis claiming he had seen a preview of the event, and that the demo would "blow people's minds."

Pras Subramanian is Lead Auto Reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram .

articles.title: Can Zimbabwe’s ZiG win trust and replace the US dollar?
articles.summary: After repeated currency crises, Zimbabweans remain wary of the ZiG.
articles.body:
Harare, Zimbabwe – The government is trying to persuade citizens to use its own currency more widely, with the longer-term aim of reducing reliance on the US dollar. But after years of currency instability, many remain reluctant to trust the latest attempt.

The Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG), introduced in April 2024, is a government effort to restore confidence in the local currency. The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) says the currency is backed by foreign currency and precious metal reserves, including gold.

Yet the challenge extends beyond introducing a new currency or strengthening its reserves. Zimbabweans who have watched their savings lose value and their wages shrink through successive currency crises remain cautious about holding money in a currency whose purchasing power they fear could deteriorate.

Zimbabwe abandoned its local currency in 2009 after a period of hyperinflation and adopted a multicurrency system dominated by the US dollar. A domestic currency returned in 2018, but repeated instability has made rebuilding public confidence difficult.

For primary school teacher Charles Mbwandarikwa, the experience of earlier currency crises remains a warning.

He receives about a third of his salary in ZiG and says he exchanges it quickly rather than holding on to it. His caution stems from the losses he suffered when Zimbabwe’s previous currency collapsed.

He lost his pension savings during the 2009 crisis. When the local currency was reintroduced in 2018, he says, the value of his salary fell from the equivalent of $540 to $40 by the end of that year.

Such experiences help explain why official assurances about the ZiG have not necessarily translated into confidence among earners.

The RBZ has sought to strengthen the currency’s credibility. On April 7 , the bank introduced an upgraded series of ZiG banknotes with revised designs and security features.

According to the RBZ, annual ZiG inflation stood at 3.7 percent last month. But relatively low inflation alone does not guarantee that people will choose to save in the currency or use it for everyday transactions.

Economist Cornelius Dube says demand for the ZiG remains weak.

“ZiG has to be available in a ratio relative to its demand. Demand for ZiG is currently very subdued,” he says.

For businesses, the currency’s acceptance by customers is a practical test of whether it can gain a larger role in the economy.

Sesedzai Chigumira, a clothing retailer, says she has made only a handful of sales in ZiG. Her experience reflects the difficulty in encouraging wider use of a currency when customers and businesses remain more comfortable transacting in US dollars.

The government’s push to reduce dollar dependence also faces a broader challenge: the existence of gold and other mineral resources does not, by itself, guarantee confidence in a currency. People must believe that it will retain its value and remain useful for paying for goods, meeting expenses and saving for the future.

Where businesses expect customers to prefer dollars, they may be reluctant to price goods or accept payments in ZiG. Consumers, in turn, have little incentive to hold the local currency if they fear that its value could fall.

That creates a cycle that policy measures alone may struggle to break.

The RBZ has moved away from its previous target of adopting a single currency by 2030, instead outlining a gradual, market-led transition towards greater use of the ZiG. The approach depends on sustained macroeconomic stability and conditions that encourage businesses and consumers to use the currency voluntarily.

The central bank has also sought to expand the ZiG’s role in domestic transactions, including through its use in tax payments and public-sector transactions, alongside measures affecting the foreign exchange and national payments systems.

But wider use in payments is not the same as confidence in a currency as a store of value. People may use ZiG when required or when circumstances leave them little choice without being willing to keep their savings in it.

For Mbwandarikwa, the memory of losing his pension savings remains part of the calculation. For Chigumira, the limited number of customers paying in ZiG shows how far the currency still has to go to become a routine part of business.

Dube says de-dollarisation is possible, but it cannot be achieved overnight. “History shows that it is possible to de-dollarise, though it’s not easy. It takes time,” he says.

For Zimbabweans who have lived through repeated currency crises, the test will be whether the ZiG can preserve their earnings and savings over time. Expanding its use through policy may be possible, but persuading people to trust it will require sustained stability and confidence in the currency.

“Policy should not try to force a conversion but should create the necessary incentives which will eventually see both businesses and consumers being indifferent to holding ZiG or US dollars,” Dube says.

articles.title: Tesla unveils Roadster featuring compressed air thrusters for limited flight
articles.summary: Tesla finally unveiled the long-awaited Roadster on Thursday night.
articles.body:
After a two-week delay, the Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster event went off with a massive bang — a flying one.

The wedge-shaped, cyberpunk-looking Roadster EV appeared in front of an inverted half roller coaster ramp erected at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas. The Roadster cruised halfway up — glued to the ramp using a vacuum fan system — then launched off the ramp upside down and performed flips in the air, using air thrusters to right itself and land on the tarmac.

Then the Roadster performed a similar stunt, jumping over several Teslas (including a semi), inverted itself, and then used its thrusters to land — an automaker first. "Well, it worked," CEO Elon Musk deadpanned.

The Roadster also went 0-60 mph in less than 1 second (0.81 seconds) during a test Tesla conducted at the event. While Tesla claimed the car could hit a top speed of 230 mph, Musk boasted that the production version could target half the speed of sound, or Mach 0.5 (383 mph).

So when can you expect to get one? "We enter production in 2028," Musk said.

Tesla said the car comes in three configurations:

Performance: road-ready, seats 2, with multi-mode suction system for next-level performance on and off track;

Thrust: race-ready, seats 2, with multi-mode suction system and rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters that enable 0–60 in <1 second

Rocket: air-ready, seats 1, with multi-mode suction system, plus perimeter-mounted cold-gas thrusters for forward, upward acceleration and lateral rotational movement. So ... yes, it can fly.

Tesla said the three versions had a range exceeding 300 miles, with a top speed of up to 230 mph for the Rocket version. Officially, in terms of performance, 0- 60 mph across the range is <1.6 seconds for Performance, <0.9 seconds for Thrust, and <0.59 seconds for Rocket.

No word yet on how the Rocket version, with its thrusters that allow short flights, would be allowed on public roads.

The event came two weeks after the initial Oct. 1 reveal date. Tesla said the reveal was pushed back due to weather conditions at the demo site, SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Rocket Development and Testing facility in Waco, Texas .

Tesla is asking prospective buyers to put down a $5,000 deposit, followed by a $45,000 wire transfer due within 10 days of the initial deposit.

Tesla has not said how much the new Roadster will cost, though it is expected to exceed $250,000.

Tesla bull Gene Munster of Deepwater Management had two big takeaways from tonight's Roadster event. "1. It was an engineering flex with no commercial value beyond embarrassing traditional car makers. 2. Elon can't wait to bring Tesla and SpaceX together," he posted on X.com .

articles.title: Oil prices dip marginally as US weighs easing sanctions on ‘shadow fleet’ tankers
articles.summary: Oil prices fell slightly on Friday as investors weighed rising tensions in the Middle East against the possibility of the US easing restrictions on ships
articles.body: Oil prices fell slightly on Friday as investors weighed rising tensions in the Middle East against the possibility of the US easing restrictions on ships carrying oil from sanctioned countries. Brent crude stood at $105.40, a decline of 0.52% while WTI crude was trading at $97.31, down 66 cents, or 0.67%.The dip came after a sharp rise in US crude prices during the previous session. WTI settled more than 3% higher on Thursday, supported by a significant reduction in US crude inventories. Brent, however, finished the session with little change.Efforts to increase supplies have also failed to fully ease market concerns. On Thursday, the International Energy Agency agreed to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel, alongside any oil left over from the record emergency reserve release announced in March. The move was intended to increase availability and bring down soaring prices.Another major factor under consideration is a possible change in US sanctions policy. The Trump administration is discussing whether to lift restrictions on certain vessels in the so-called “shadow fleet”, which has carried oil and petroleum products from Russia, Iran and Venezuela, a US official said on Wednesday, as cited by Reuters. The proposed step is aimed at easing record-high global freight rates.The deliberations follow US President Donald Trump’s temporary lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel fuel. The decision prompted criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some Republicans in the US Senate.Developments in the Middle East, meanwhile, continue to put pressure on the market. The intensifying conflict involving Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis, along with fresh attacks on ships in the region, has provided support to oil prices.Attacks around the waterway have increased over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is intensifying strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and stricter sanctions imposed last month.The violence also spread to Yemen’s southern city of Aden on Thursday, when the Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex, killing two guards. articles.title: Fairfax’s plan: Bring Digit, IIFL Cap under IDBI Bank
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Canadian financial group Fairfax plans to consolidate its holdings in insurance and capital markets under IDBI Bank after being selected as the
articles.body: MUMBAI: Canadian financial group Fairfax plans to consolidate its holdings in insurance and capital markets under IDBI Bank after being selected as the strategic buyer for a 60.7% stake in the lender for Rs 52,878 crore, creating a financial services group spanning banking, insurance, investment banking and wealth management.Fairfax proposes to transfer its interests in Go Digit Life Insurance and Go Digit General Insurance, collectively known as Digit, to IDBI Bank. It also plans to contribute its interest in IIFL Capital Services, which provides investment banking and wealth management services.The proposed transfers would be undertaken at the respective market prices of the businesses and would require regulatory approvals. Fairfax had invested in IIFL in 2015 and subsequently partnered Kamesh Goyal to launch Go Digit general and life insurance.The group also outlined plans for the leadership of the combined bank. Rakesh Sharma, IDBI Bank's current managing director and CEO, is expected to continue leading its operations. Fairfax plans to bring CVR Rajendran, former CEO of CSB Bank, into the leadership team and appoint NS Kannan, former CEO of ICICI Prudential Life and CFO of ICICI Bank, as chairman, subject to RBI approval.The proposed transfers are not expected to change the management or operating structures of Digit or IIFL Capital. Digit will continue to be led by founder and chairman Goyal, while IIFL Capital's management team, led by R Venkataraman, Vasudev Jagannath and Nemkumar H, will continue to run its capital markets, investment banking, wealth and asset management and mutual fund distribution businesses.Fairfax plans to consolidate its banking, insurance and capital markets businesses under IDBI Bank, combining the lender with Digit and IIFL Capital to expand its financial services reach and boost India's credit-to-GDP ratio. articles.title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, eyes on Warsh
articles.summary: Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day's tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, with traders also awaiting comments from Federal R...
articles.body:
Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day's tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, with traders also awaiting comments from Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh at the IMF's annual gathering.

Seoul and Tokyo enjoyed healthy gains in early exchanges, with chipmakers SK hynix and Kioxia among the best performers -- having been pummelled Thursday as investors bailed out of the once-dominant AI sector.

The selling had been fuelled by forecast-beating US inflation data that ramped up bets on more Fed interest rate hikes, as well as concerns about the financial health of data centre operator CoreWeave owing to its huge debt pile.

The New Jersey firm -- which has borrowed heavily to finance hefty purchases of pricey semiconductor chips from Nvidia -- tanked 15.5 percent Wednesday as yields on some of its bonds soared, reflecting heightened angst over its future.

That added to concerns about the whole AI-tech complex, but Nvidia chief Jensen Huang on Thursday lifted spirits by defending the company and its health.

"CoreWeave's strength is improving every day," he told Bloomberg. "I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."

CoreWeave's shares climbed almost six percent.

Huang's "defence of CoreWeave's financial position was enough to pull the NeoCloud complex off the floor, drag AI equities higher and give the broader market something resembling a pulse", wrote SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes.

"One moment the market was pricing the possibility that the AI financing machine had started eating its own tail, the next it was listening to the high priest of the boom explain that the patient was getting stronger.

"AI Jesus had entered the trading room and, for a while at least, the machines found religion again."

Seoul jumped more than two percent and Tokyo around 1.8 percent, though they slumped 7.6 percent and 4.9 percent respectively Thursday.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei and Manila were also well up.

Traders are now awaiting comments at the International Monetary Fund's gathering in Bangkok, with hopes that he will give some insight into policymakers' thinking following this week's inflation-busting consumer inflation data.

The reading was the highest in five months and saw investors push up bets on a second-successive rate hike this month.

articles.title: Tesla unveils what it says is a flying car
articles.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk Thursday unveiled a car that he said will be able to fly, a feature long relegated to science fiction and Saturday morning cartoons.
articles.body: Tesla CEO Elon Musk Thursday unveiled a car that he said will be able to fly, a feature long relegated to science fiction and Saturday morning cartoons. At a product reveal at a Texas test facility belonging to SpaceX, Musk’s other public company, he showed off Tesla’s new Roadster, a two-person sports car that not only could go from 0 to 60 mph in record time of less than a second, but he said used suction underneath the car to climb up a steep ramp and hang upside down before spinning off the ramp, flipping in the air and using air jets to land. The car did not have an actual driver during the demonstration, which was done “to make sure we don’t kill anyone,” Musk told the crowd. “Success is not guaranteed,” he said. “I mean that. It’ll probably work, but if it doesn’t work, we’re at a safe distance.” Later in Thursday’s demonstration, the Roadster used the same jets to leap over a line of Tesla’s existing models parked side-by-side, and then used the jets off the back of the car to accelerate to 60 mph in that record time. But even with the success of the staged event, whether the car will actually be able to live up to the promise and provide owners with the ability to both fly rather than just hop, while also being able to drive very fast on roads, remains to be proven. The car uses 10 nozzles and what Musk described as “ultra high-pressure air tanks” to propel itself, both in the air, and to accelerate quickly when on the ground. He described the technology as “the results of what happens when you have a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company.” He said the car will go into production in 2028, although throughout Tesla’s history, Musk has made promises about when things would be accomplish, only to miss that timeline by a number of years. Musk told an enthusiastic crowd of Tesla fans “we need an audience to prove that it’s not AI or SI. So you guys can tell people you saw it with your eyes, because what you see with your eyes, you will not believe.” And whether the car is able to truly fly is very difficult to say, despite Thursday night’s demonstration. It certainly didn’t have any demonstration of long-range flight. In recent years, there have been many advancements in electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, known as eVTOL’s. While there are some working models, there are still many engineering roadblocks to road-worthy cars that can truly fly. “Aircraft are extremely sensitive to weight, whereas with ground vehicles you want them to have bumpers and crumple zones and all that,” Roger Connor, curator for vertical flight at the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum, told CNN Thursday before the event. “Inevitably, something that is a hybrid between the two is going to be a poor performing aircraft and a poor performing vehicle, and also quite expensive.” One car that is in development, made by California start-up Alef, has been able to get airborne using eight propellers, four in the front and four in the back. But the vehicle weighs 254 pounds, a small fraction of the weight of a Tesla Roadster. It can also only carry one person which must weigh less than the vehicle itself. Ahead of Tesla’s demonstration, Alef CEO Jim Dukhovny told CNN that he wouldn’t be surprised if Tesla was able to get its Roadster off the ground during the event. But that doesn’t mean it can truly “fly.” “It absolutely is 100% feasible,” he said. “That being said, the hardest part on all eVTOLs, and for us, it’s a transition from (rising) vertical to (moving) forward. It needs to be extremely careful, making sure you do not lose lift, and making sure it’s very stable.” Conner also expressed doubt that any street legal car like a Roadster would be able to fly anywhere an owner might want it to go. “We’re not talking about sustained flight,” he said. “We are literally talking about hopping.”

articles.body: MUMBAI: Markets regulator Sebi on Thursday revised the process for Closing Auction Session (CAS) that included changing the trading timings and how the settlement prices of stocks and indices would be arrived at for derivatives contracts, a Sebi circular said.Under the changed rules, there will be a 10-minute CAS that will start at 3:30 pm and end at 3:40 pm on all trading days. At the same time, trading in index and stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm, except for index derivatives contracts on the expiry day.Sebi also brought in a major change relating to how the settlement prices of expiring derivatives contracts are calculated. This will now be based on a Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) methodology using the last 30 minutes of continuous trading.Order entry for both limit and market orders will be allowed from 3:31 pm to 3:36 pm, followed by a period during which only limit orders can be placed. The session will close randomly between 3:38 pm and 3:40 pm.The post-close session in the cash segment will run from 3:50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing prices of securities.Earlier, since the introduction of CAS in Aug, this was based on prices arrived through the CAS process. After CAS was enforced, during several sessions, wild swings in index levels and stock prices were seen.After this, and also after Sebi’s investigations found some brokers were manipulating the system, the regulator issued another consultation paper.Post that, Sebi also had discussions with its Secondary Market Advisory Committee and with the stock exchanges. It also went through the several thousand comments it received on its proposals. Sebi introduced CAS in India with the objective of improving transparency and price discovery while ensuring a more orderly closing process.The new changes would be implemented in two phases, between Dec 7 and Feb 8, 2027, the Sebi release saidYou use AI every day. articles.title: Elon Musk's monopoly charge, Reliance's response: What's the Starlink-Jio row all about?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Reliance Industries has welcomed Elon Musk’s Starlink to India, saying it has never feared competition and that its own satellite services are
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Reliance Industries has welcomed Elon Musk’s Starlink to India, saying it has never feared competition and that its own satellite services are also in the queue.The statement comes as a response to Musk’s repeated allegations that vested interests were obstructing Starlink’s entry into India. Reliance, however, stressed that all companies must comply with Indian laws and regulations, adding that priority is to serve the people.In a statement released on Friday, the company said India’s investment and innovation landscape was open to both domestic and foreign players, with the same regulatory process applying to all applicants.The statement, posted on social media platform X, stated, “In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record. Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people. That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances.”The telecom firm further added, “At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best. Jio itself entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 as the newest player, with not a single customer. In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world. We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink. Every player, Jio included, must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land.”Musk accuses Reliance of opposing Starlink’s entryReliance’s statement came after SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk accused the Indian conglomerate of benefiting from the existing market structure and alleged that arguments against Starlink’s entry were contradictory.In a post on X, Musk had said, "The ridiculous arguments by Ambani’s army of Internet shills make no sense. On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole."Musk argued that greater competition would give Indian consumers more choices, even if it reduced the profits of existing players. However, he said, this would not necessarily threaten their businesses."The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," he wrote.Musk had previously alleged monopolistic practices in India’s telecommunications market and questioned the regulatory barriers facing Starlink’s commercial launch in the country.In another post, he directly addressed the government, writing, "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?"The government has denied Musk’s allegation that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.Government asks Starlink to comply with lawUnion communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has said that there is no question of allowing a monopoly in satellite communications. He also said three entities are in line for final approval for commercial licences.Scindia said that India was close to taking a final decision on the pricing framework for satellite communication services. All licensed operators, including Starlink, must meet security requirements before beginning commercial operations.Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch its services in India because it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to establish domestic infrastructure, a senior government official said earlier this week.The government has no objection to the company rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations, sources said.A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the “first hop”, connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to establish base stations is intended to help authorities ensure compliance with the law.Reliance Jio, Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Musk’s Starlink are the three entities planning to launch satellite communication services in India.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal has also said that Airtel’s satellite venture, Eutelsat OneWeb, could receive regulatory approval before Starlink because it applied earlier and is further along in the process.You use AI every day. articles.title: She received Rs 9.04 lakh leave encashment on retiring from LIC; taxman allowed only Rs 3 lakh exemption, but ITAT Jaipur grants relief even after  1,277-day appeal delay
articles.summary: How much of your leave encashment is exempt from income tax? That depends on whether you are a government employee or a private sector employee.
articles.body: How much of your leave encashment is exempt from income tax? That depends on whether you are a government employee or a private sector employee. The limit for private sector employees was recently raised to Rs 25 lakh.In one case, a retired woman faced a tax notice on her leave encashment, with the Income Tax Department allowing only part of it for exemption. Read on to know why she won relief from ITAT.What the case is aboutA woman retired from Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) on June 30, 2020 after more than 30 years of service. She received Rs 9.04 lakh as leave encashment, in addition to her other retirement benefits. While filing her income tax return (ITR), she claimed a tax exemption on the entire leave encashment amount.Also Read | Taxpayer declared Rs 1.79 lakh in ITR, faced Rs 11.22 crore income addition on large cash deposits, unsecured loans; ITAT grants him chance to substantiate case with condition he plant 500 treesShe was unaware that LIC employees fall under the category of non-government employees for this purpose. Under the rules applicable in 2020, she was eligible for a tax exemption of only Rs 3 lakh on leave encashment, rather than the full Rs 9.04 lakh she had claimed. The exemption limit for leave encashment received by non-government employees was raised to Rs 25 lakh in Budget 2023.The Income Tax Department restricted her exemption to Rs 3 lakh and sought to tax the balance of Rs 6.04 lakh. This led to an income tax notice being issued to her.In her application seeking condonation of delay, the woman explained that she had entrusted the matter to a tax consultant. According to her, the consultant did not file the appeal before the tribunal or inform her that the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) had dismissed her case. She said she learnt about the order after receiving a substantial tax demand.As a result, she approached the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Jaipur, only after a delay of around 1,277 days, engaging a new chartered accountant to pursue the matter.The Income Tax Department opposed her request, arguing that she had not established “sufficient cause” for such a long delay.The tribunal first had to decide whether her explanation justified condoning the delay and then consider whether the higher exemption limit applied to her leave encashment.On September 28, 2026, Mrs Moongia won the case before the ITAT Jaipur.Also Read | Woman paid Rs 79 lakh for a Rs 2.14 crore villa, but construction remained unfinished; Telangana RERA orders full refund with 10.7% interest and fines builder Rs 1.03 croreWhy did the retired woman win relief?The ITAT Jaipur accepted her request to condone the delay of 1,277 days. It observed that the law recognises that an individual should not be held responsible for a mistake or negligence committed by a tax consultant hired to handle their tax matters. A taxpayer should not have to suffer because of an error made by their consultant.On the delay, the tribunal considered Moongia's explanation that she had relied on her tax consultant to handle the proceedings. It observed that a professional handling a client's tax case was expected to communicate important developments, including the dismissal of an appeal, and advise the client on the next steps.The tribunal stated that “mistake or negligence on the part of a tax consultant engaged by the assessee cannot be attributed to the assessee and he/she should not be made to suffer.” It also referred to the Supreme Court's decision in Collector, Land Acquisition v. Mst Katiji, which supports a liberal approach to condoning delays in appropriate cases.Also Read | He moved to the US for a job and forgot to file his India ITR; taxman imposed Rs 8.29 lakh penalty, but ITAT Jaipur cancelled it for this reasonAfter considering her explanation, the tribunal held that there was “sufficient cause” to condone the delay of 1,277 days. It therefore admitted the appeal for consideration on its merits.The tax dispute concerned the exemption ceiling under Section 10(10AA). The tax authorities had relied on the Rs 3 lakh limit, while the woman’s representative cited CBDT Notification No. 31/2023, dated May 24, 2023, which raised the exemption limit for eligible employees to Rs 25 lakh.The Jaipur tribunal also considered earlier ITAT decisions that had applied the revised limit. It noted that a coordinate bench had already ruled in favour of allowing leave encashment exemption within the Rs 25 lakh ceiling.Explaining its conclusion, the tribunal said: “In view of this legal position, we are in respectful agreement of what has been held by the afore cited coordinate Jaipur Benches of this Tribunal as noted hereinabove.”Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additionsIt ultimately held that the woman was eligible for exemption on the Rs 9,04,669 she had received.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that leave encashment paid to central and state government employees upon retirement is completely exempt from income tax. However, employees working in the private sector and other non-government organisations are eligible for exemption only up to the limits laid down under the income-tax law.Surana said any leave encashment received beyond the eligible exemption limit is taxable under the head “salaries” in the year in which the payment is received. The excess amount is taxed at the normal income-tax slab rates applicable to the employee, with no separate or special tax rate for leave encashment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: India raises petrol export duty fivefold to Rs 2.5/litre, cuts diesel levy to Rs 8.5
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The government has raised the export duty on petrol fivefold to Rs 2.5 per litre from Rs 0.5, while cutting the levy on diesel to Rs 8.5 per
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The government has raised the export duty on petrol fivefold to Rs 2.5 per litre from Rs 0.5, while cutting the levy on diesel to Rs 8.5 per litre from Rs 16. The revised rates came into effect on October 16.The export duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) remains unchanged at Rs 10.5 per litre, according to a finance ministry notification issued on Friday.The revised rates cover the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED), with no road and infrastructure cess (RIC) applicable on exports of petrol, diesel and ATF. The changes follow the previous revision, which took effect on October 1.Export duties on the three petroleum products are reviewed every fortnight, with rates determined by average international prices of crude oil and the respective fuels during the period since the last review. The latest revision changes the levies on petrol and diesel in opposite directions, while leaving the ATF duty unchanged.The revised export duties will not affect the existing excise duty rates on petrol and diesel sold for domestic consumption.India initially introduced windfall taxes on fuel exports in July 2022, before withdrawing them two years later. The government brought the levy back in March 2026 as crude oil prices surged during the US-Israeli war on Iran.The tax was intended to discourage exports and protect domestic supplies of petroleum products amid the conflict in the Middle East. It was also aimed at preventing exporters from benefiting unduly from differences between domestic and international prices as global crude oil prices rose.The government imposed export duties on diesel and ATF on March 27, 2026, and introduced the levy on petrol exports from May 16. Rates have since been reviewed every fortnight.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Deja el almacén para conducir camiones de basura y ganar 11.500 euros más al año: "Cualquiera con brazos y piernas puede hacerlo"
articles.standfirst: Luca Klimmt, de 32 años, explica satisfecha su cambio laboral
articles.summary: Luca Klimmt, de 32 años, explica satisfecha su cambio laboral
articles.body: La joven británica Luca Klimmt, de 32 años, decidió dejar el almacén donde trabajaba. Quería más ingresos y nuevos retos profesionales. Empezó conduciendo una furgoneta, pero sabía que si obtenía la licencia de camiones podría recibir un mayor salario. Finalmente, logró su objetivo en octubre de 2023 y ahora conduce un enorme camión de la basura de la marca Volvo de diez metros de longitud. Ha conseguido, con este cambio, un incremento salarial neto de 11.500 euros anuales al cambio. "A veces la gente da por hecho que tengo un conductor hombre en la cabina, pero tengo que decirles que trabajo sola y que lo hago todo por mi cuenta. Hay gente que me ha preguntado si realmente conduzco yo el camión o si voy acompañada. A muchos les sorprende cuando les explico que voy a los mandos del camión", ha afirmado Luca Klimmt en declaraciones recogidas por Ladbible. En el trabajo, de todas formas, no recibe ningún tipo de comentario ni afronta prejuicios. "Todos me tratan por igual. Todos tenemos los mismos brazos y piernas, cualquiera puede conducir un camión si está preparado para hacerlo. Es como conducir un coche", ha argumentado la británica. El incremento salarial que ha experimentado es notable, pero su jornada laboral no es sencilla. Esta joven británica de 32 años debe levantarse todos los días temprano para empezar su jornada a las 5 de la madrugada. Además, su turno de trabajo implica conducir durante unos 400 kilómetros al día. Pese al esfuerzo inicial que supuso afrontar este desgaste al principio, Luca Klimmt está ahora encantada con el cambio laboral. De hecho, la joven británica ha aconsejado al resto de mujeres a perder el posible miedo a formar parte de este sector. "Me gustaría ver a más mujeres aquí. Mi consejo es que lo intenten, que no hay nada que temer", ha comentado.

articles.title: FM Sitharaman seeks early India-US trade deal, flags China’s market access barriers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has called for an early conclusion of the India-US trade agreement, stressing its importance for bilateral
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has called for an early conclusion of the India-US trade agreement, stressing its importance for bilateral economic relations and global trade.Her remarks come a day after commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the trade pact had been finalised and was currently undergoing legal drafting."I think recently the Indian commerce minister has also spoken that they expect and wish to have the agreement signed soon. Negotiations have been going on. I hope, in the interest of global trade and in the interest of trade between the two partners, India and US, the trade agreement gets concluded at the earliest," she said on Friday.FM Sitharaman also raised concerns over India's trade relationship with China, particularly the growing imbalance and the difficulties Indian businesses face in accessing the Chinese market.Despite years of engagement with Beijing, India has made little headway in securing greater market access for several products, including generic medicines, bovine meat, vegetables and other perishable goods, she said.Speaking to the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, the finance minister pointed to non-tariff restrictions as a key impediment to trade between the two countries."Non-tariff barriers are the biggest hurdle in the trade between India and China," she said. China had continued to use phytosanitary measures and other non-tariff restrictions, she added, despite the possibility of addressing these issues through discussions and investigations.Sitharaman said India had chosen negotiations over punitive tariffs as a means of tackling substantial trade imbalances with its trading partners, even if reaching a resolution took time.BRICS should focus on people's welfareOn BRICS, minister Sitharaman rejected the view that the grouping's purpose was to counter another country or bloc. Instead, she said, its focus should be on strengthening cooperation for the benefit of its people."I don't think BRICS's intention is to counter others. It is more to strengthen the partnership through the BRICS," she added.She highlighted the grouping's scale, noting that its member countries represented nearly 40 per cent of the world's population. Greater cooperation among them could support trade, improve mutual understanding and open up economic opportunities, she said.Sitharaman also pointed to the expanding membership of BRICS, with 11 to 12 countries actively engaging with one another and collectively accounting for around 45 per cent of global trade.Infrastructure spending has helped sustain India's growthTurning to the domestic economy, Sitharaman said India had maintained strong growth despite disruptions across the world. The country had been the fastest-growing major economy over the previous four to five years, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic, she said.She credited this performance to a combination of inclusive growth, improved access to resources, skill development for young people, fiscal prudence and higher public capital expenditure.The finance minister emphasised the role of infrastructure investment in supporting economic activity, saying it had a stronger multiplier effect than directly transferring an equivalent amount of money to people. Such investment also generated employment, she said.According to Sitharaman, public expenditure on infrastructure allows money to reach people through the economic activity it creates, while avoiding the same degree of pressure on the fiscal deficit that some other forms of spending could entail.She also linked government borrowing to the creation of infrastructure assets, arguing that the approach had delivered economic benefits. "Borrowing goes for asset creation, and as a result, the economy has benefited," she said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Air India has cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 20, as the situation in Saudi Arabia continues to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Air India has cancelled all flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 20, as the situation in Saudi Arabia continues to evolve. The airline said that it is monitoring developments and assessing the situation to ensure flights could resume safely.“In view of the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia, all Air India flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah stand cancelled until 20 October 2026. We are closely monitoring developments and continuously assessing the situation to ensure the safe resumption of operations.”Referring to refunds due to the cancellation, the aviation giant said, “Passengers affected by these cancellations are being offered a full refund. At Air India, the safety and security of our passengers and crew remain the highest priority.”The latest cancellations follow flight disruptions announced last week, when Air India, Akasa Air and IndiGo suspended or reduced flights to Riyadh after reports of explosions, including a loud blast at the city's international airport.How to get a refund for cancelled Air India flightsPassengers affected by the cancellations can request a refund by following these steps:Website or app bookings: Visit Air India’s Manage Booking section to request a refund.Travel agent or third-party website bookings: Contact the agent or website to initiate the refund.Ticketing office bookings: Visit the same Air India office where you purchased the ticket to request a refund.Checking refund status: For bookings made and cancelled through Air India’s website or app, visit the refund support portal and select ‘Status Check on Pending Refund’. For other bookings, contact the respective agent, website or ticketing office.Refund credit: The amount will be credited to the account used to pay for the booking. If that account is closed or invalid, provide your new bank details to an Air India agent at the ticketing office.More carriers halt Saudi servicesSeveral other international airlines have also changed their schedules amid the conflict.Air France-KLM has extended the suspension of flights to and from Riyadh until the end of October. Akasa Air has suspended services to and from Jeddah and Riyadh until October 17, while IndiGo has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah until the same date.Etihad Airways has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, along with 10 flights to Dammam and Jeddah, until October 19. Gulf Air has cancelled flights to and from Riyadh from October 12 to October 17, while Lufthansa Group airlines have cancelled all flights to Riyadh until October 16.Malaysia Airlines has cancelled flights to and from Jeddah and Madinah until October 17 as a precaution. Philippine Airlines has extended the suspension of its Riyadh flights until November 29, while Qatar Airways has temporarily suspended flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam.Other airlines have pushed back their plans to resume services. Cathay Pacific has postponed the resumption of its Hong Kong-Dubai and Hong Kong-Riyadh routes until January 31, 2027. Delta Air Lines has delayed its planned flights from Atlanta to Riyadh until March 2027.Air India sets up team to cut costsMeanwhile, Air India has set up a team to find ways to reduce costs across the airline as it faces rising operating pressures. Its new CEO, Tewolde Gebremariam, has asked employees to focus on spending carefully and taking responsibility for their work.In a message to staff on October 12, he said, "A multidisciplinary, cross-functional Cost Savings Team has been established on full-time basis to identify cost-saving opportunities across the organisation,"The team will review spending across departments and look for ways to save money, he said."Ongoing airspace closures, the conflict in the Middle East and its resulting operational disruptions, and persistently high jet fuel costs continue to place significant pressure on airlines across the industry," he said.Air India, jointly owned by the Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, reported a consolidated loss of Rs 22,238.23 crore in the 2025-26 financial year.Meanwhile, the Middle East conflict has now continued for more than seven months, keeping airlines and oil markets on edge.You use AI every day. articles.title: Oil eases, but set for weekly gain on Mideast supply risks
articles.summary: By Sam Li and Siyi Liu BEIJING/SINGAPORE, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Oil prices eased on Friday but were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East sup...
articles.body:
BEIJING/SINGAPORE, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Oil prices eased on Friday but were heading for weekly gains on uncertainty over Middle East supplies and a larger-than-expected draw from crude stockpiles in ‌the United States.

Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.47%, to $105.42 a barrel by 0623 GMT, while ‌US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 49 cents, or 0.50%, to $97.48.

WTI settled up more than 3% on Thursday after a big US ​crude stock draw on hurricane production shut-ins.

For this week so far, Brent increased 0.49%, while WTI jumped 5.91%.

"Uncertainty in the Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz has the market pricing in a significant risk premium," ING analysts wrote in a note.

Some kind of agreement between the US and Iran was required to ‌provide more confidence to the market that ⁠stronger oil flows from the region would continue, they added.

Supply jitters also increased as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was ⁠stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.

Total Hormuz clearance averaged 11.62 million barrels per day over the seven days to October 13, about 68% of the 17.15 million bpd baseline, said ship ​tracking ​firm Kpler.

"Intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower," Kpler ​analysts said in a report on Thursday, adding ‌that they expected a slower and more uneven Hormuz recovery in the absence of a comprehensive political deal.

The Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict.

The International Energy Agency agreed on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market and any oil remaining from a record ‌release of emergency reserves pledged in March to boost supply and ​cool soaring prices.

During the previous trading session, oil prices rose overnight in ​a sign that "investors were dissatisfied with these measures," ​Haitong Futures said in a note.

"What would really cool the oil market is an easing ‌of tensions in the Middle East."

The Trump administration is ​considering lifting sanctions on some ​so-called shadow fleet vessels that have carried oil and petroleum products from countries such as Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in a bid to cut record global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
